page: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor, running under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, reaching clock frequencies up to 4.5 GHz. The CPU features 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, as well as hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The configuration includes 128.0 GB of system memory, delivering a 2.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, paired with 3780 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local temporary storage. No discrete graphics processors are included.

Synthetic benchmarks highlight exceptional raw computational capabilities and instruction throughput. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 26926.0 and a single-core score of 2856.0, placing both in the top 10% tier. Clang software compilation reached 63108.0, and PassMark CPU testing registered 91889.21. Memory subsystems demonstrate high read and write throughput, measuring 205.53 GB/sec and 131.87 GB/sec in large-block transfers respectively, which supports intensive I/O operations alongside the bundled high-capacity NVMe SSD.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution creates a focused compute profile rather than a standard general-purpose memory layout. This architectural balance yields high compute density per allocated core, making the hardware cost-efficient for CPU-bound tasks where large memory footprints are unnecessary. However, memory-intensive datasets exceeding 128 GB are constrained unless distributed. Workload performance shines in software compilation, batch text and image processing, high-throughput static web serving, local NVMe caching, and small-to-medium parameter CPU-based LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is an x86_64 cloud server powered by a 4.5 GHz AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivering 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores. It features 128.0 GB of RAM, a 2.0 GB per-vCPU ratio, and includes 3780 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage without discrete GPUs. Hardware support encompasses AVX-512 instruction sets with VNNI and BF16 extensions. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong computational capabilities, achieving top-decile Geekbench results (2856.0 single-core, 26926.0 multi-core) and robust multi-threaded compression metrics. The server yields solid cost efficiency for CPU-dense processing jobs that do not require deep memory pools, trading extensive RAM allocation for heightened compute density and fast local scratch storage. Microsoft Azure D64alds_v7 is well suited for code compilation pipelines, web serving, database indexing, and quantized machine learning inference.
